notes: §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR1: the selected items of identifier-1 are moved to those of identifier-2 and "The results are the same as if the user had referred to each pair of corresponding identifiers in separate MOVE statements"; GR2: "Any length evaluation or subscripting associated with identifier-2 is evaluated immediately before the data is moved to the respective data item". CorrespondingBinder.Bind selects the pairs (CorrMatch) and binds each as an ordinary MOVE (MoveBinder.BindMoveOf), CorrespondingEmitter.Emit renders them in declaration order, and below 2002 CorrAccess anchors no group local, so each pair re-identifies the group (kb/Work PB5185). A subscript whose data-name lies in a REDEFINED record binds through the position route as a statement-level temporary (SubscriptBinder.MaterializePosition): since kb/Work PB5767 (wave 20262068) the MOVE's identification steps are taken off the statement's pre-op queue (BoundCorresponding.PairIdentification) and re-run before each pair, so refute-a/m-send-two.cob prints CORR 29 (the separate MOVEs in declaration order), m-recv-two.cob [21111211], m-two-sub-rr.cob 21B, at 85; 2002 and 2023 still freeze (22, [22111111], 23A). Witness pb5767_move_corresponding_redefined_subscript_per_pair_85 (SEND 29, RECV 21111211). The later editions require the freeze (§2002:14.8.24.3 GR6, §2023:14.9.25.4 GR11: "the subscript value used is that resulting from the evaluation of the subscript at the start of the execution of the statement").

next.reason: 1985 GR1: the results are 'the same as if the user had referred to each pair of corresponding identifiers in separate MOVE statements', so each implied MOVE evaluates its own subscripts. §2023:14.9.25.4 GR11 keeps that equivalence 'except that if subscripting is specified for identifier-3 or identifier-4, the subscript value used is that resulting from the evaluation of the subscript at the start of the execution of the statement'. A conforming 1985 program can observe it: MOVE CORR A (I OF B) TO B, where B and the table element A each contain an item I, alters the subscript mid-statement; 1985 re-evaluates it for later pairs, 2023 does not. 1985 GR2's once-only rule is format 1's only. §2023:14.9.25.3 SR13 states the sending/receiving roles of the corresponding items.
